title: Kaido Racer
notes: Genki games: the car models were decoded from scratch (the format has no public description).
Folder names are the number of the game's archive entry (no car names are known).  One car = the first (most detailed) of its levels of detail.

The car file is a tree of parts and holds EVERY variant of the shop (5 bodies, 5 front bumpers, several bonnets, wings ...); the variants of a part sit on the same place.  The car here is the stock set: the first variant of every part, each part at its place in the tree.  Moving parts (pop-up headlights) are in their closed position.  The game's hull / shadow volumes are left out.

Textures: the pictures of the game's body-part file (body, bumpers, grilles, lamps, decals); the cars of Racing Battle and Tokyo Xtreme Racer 3 come with the livery of the file, Kaido Racer / Drift with the plain white body picture (the game colours the car at run time).  Parts without a picture have the game's own material colour (black interior, tinted glass ...).
No wheels: they are separate models in the game.  The game's wheels are in the folder _Rims (most detailed version only).

Left out on purpose: stickers and number plates that the game textures at run time (blank white cards), light-glow sprites and reflection layers (Kaido Racer 1 / 2, Drift), the 4 cards behind the wheels of Kaido Racer 1.

The game's triangle strips run on from one piece to another without a break.  Racing Battle C1 GP and Kaido Racer 2 mark the joins in the vertex data (see below); Kaido Racer 1, Drift and TXR3 do not, there the converter removes a join when the two triangles around a long edge do not form a flat quad with continuous normals, or when a long triangle contradicts the normals of its corners (real long slivers such as door sills and roof bands are kept).
